title: sign() boundary derived from content hash; content containing boundary string is unguarded
description: sign() computes the MIME multipart boundary as 'boundary_from_content()' — the first 16 bytes of SHA-256(content_mime), hex-encoded, prefixed with '----=_Part_'. This is deterministic and reproducible (good for tests) but does not verify that the boundary string is absent from content_mime before using it. RFC 2046 §5.1.1 requires the boundary not appear in the body. If the content to be signed is adversarially crafted to contain the derived boundary string, the resulting multipart/signed message is malformed. This is a security-relevant input validation gap on a signing path.
